review_notes: Read the whole target file and the definition of multiPartial (Statements/MultiPartial.lean). Grepped for other uses of the zero multi-index `(fun _ => 0)` and for an existing simp lemma for it. I found none; each use re-proves the fact locally, with `simp [multiPartial]`, `rfl` or an equivalent. I did not run Lean, so I don't claim the proposed lemma compiles. The `norm_num` side goals and the `max` combination at the end of the file are not simp-interface issues.

findings.excerpt: simpa [multiPartial] using hbound x (hAsub hx).1 (hAsub hx).2 t ht i (fun _ => 0) hα0
findings.problem: There is no canonical simp lemma saying that `multiPartial g (fun _ => 0) = g`. The order-zero case is how callers extract a plain pointwise bound from a multiPartial bound. Every caller instead unfolds the definition with `simp [multiPartial]`. That exposes the `Function.iterate` composition of three `spatialPartial` iterates, which is an implementation detail, and relies on `Function.iterate_zero` simp lemmas to clean it up. The same unfolding appears in this file twice (lines 58 and 83). It also appears in AnnulusEuclideanNormBound.lean (`simpa [multiPartial, hM_abs] using h`), twice in EnergyClassLemmas.lean (`h_multiPartial_zero` proved by `simp [multiPartial]`) and in AveragedForceBound.lean (`he ... := rfl`). Because `multiPartial` stays a def with no simp interface, each use needs its own `have hα0 ... := by norm_num` and its own unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: In MultiPartial.lean, add `@[simp] theorem multiPartial_zero (g : ParabolicPoint → ℝ) : multiPartial g (fun _ => 0) = g := rfl`. The proof should be `rfl` or `by simp [multiPartial]`, because the iterates have exponent 0. Optionally add a pointwise form `multiPartial g (fun _ => 0) z = g z`. Then replace `simpa [multiPartial] using ...` with `simpa using ...` or `by simpa using hbound ... (fun _ => 0) hα0`. Replace the local `h_multiPartial_zero` and `he` lemmas by the new simp lemma. Do not make `multiPartial` itself `@[simp]`, because that would unfold the iterates everywhere.
findings.benefit: Order-zero extraction becomes a single named, stable simp rewrite, and the definition of `multiPartial` stays opaque to callers. Proofs no longer depend on how the iterates are ordered, so they survive a change of definition. At least six duplicated local proofs across the CIVAxisymmetric files can be replaced by one lemma.

evidence.excerpt: have h_multiPartial_zero : multiPartial (fun w => f w i) (fun _ => 0) = fun w => f w i := by
have he : multiPartial (fun y => f y m) (fun _ => 0) = fun y => f y m := rfl
